review_notes: I read the whole of Basic.lean and grepped the ContinuedFractions directory for uses of IntFractPair.of, mapFr, coeFn and coe_to_intFractPair. I also read the relevant parts of Translations.lean and TerminatesIffRat.lean. The only simp lemma in the target is coe_to_intFractPair, and it looks fine: it is rfl, the coercion is tagged @[coe], and the rewrite direction is canonical. The two findings concern missing projection lemmas for `of` and `mapFr`. As evidence, downstream proofs unfold the definitions by name (`simp [IntFractPair.of]`, a local `attribute [local simp] IntFractPair.mapFr`). I did not run Lean. Whether adding these lemmas would change any downstream simp call set is unchecked, and I did not search for a name clash with existing lemmas.

findings.excerpt:
protected def of (v : K) : IntFractPair K :=
  ⟨⌊v⌋, Int.fract v⟩
findings.problem: `IntFractPair.of` is the basic constructor of the whole development, but the file has no simp lemmas for its components, such as `(IntFractPair.of v).b = ⌊v⌋` and `(IntFractPair.of v).fr = Int.fract v`. Downstream proofs therefore unfold the definition by name, for example `simp [IntFractPair.of]` and `simp only [IntFractPair.of, Int.fract_intCast]`. They even re-prove the fr-projection fact locally as `have H : (IntFractPair.of v).fr = Int.fract v := by simp [IntFractPair.of]`. Unfolding by name exposes the pair literal `⟨⌊v⌋, Int.fract v⟩` and does not give the canonical form `⌊v⌋` and `Int.fract v` directly. It also forces every caller to decide whether to unfold.
findings.proposed_change: Generate projection lemmas for `of`, either by tagging the definition `@[simps]` or by writing `@[simp] theorem of_b (v : K) : (IntFractPair.of v).b = ⌊v⌋ := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem of_fr (v : K) : (IntFractPair.of v).fr = Int.fract v := rfl`. Callers can then use `simp` instead of `simp [IntFractPair.of]`. The `have H` at Translations.lean:129 becomes a plain `simp`/`rfl`. The definition should stay non-reducible and non-simp, so `of` does not unfold in general.
findings.benefit: The normal form of `(of v).b` and `(of v).fr` is stated once and fires automatically. The many ad hoc `simp [IntFractPair.of]` calls in Translations, CorrectnessTerminating and TerminatesIffRat get shorter and more predictable. They also stop depending on the internal pair representation.

evidence.excerpt: have H : (IntFractPair.of v).fr = Int.fract v := by simp [IntFractPair.of]

findings.excerpt:
def mapFr {β : Type*} (f : K → β) (gp : IntFractPair K) : IntFractPair β :=
  ⟨gp.b, f gp.fr⟩
findings.problem: `mapFr` has no simp lemmas for its projections (`(mapFr f gp).b = gp.b`, `(mapFr f gp).fr = f gp.fr`) or for `mapFr f (mk b fr)`. `coeFn` is defined from `mapFr (↑)` and the simp lemma `coe_to_intFractPair` is proved by `rfl`, so `mapFr` and the coercion have no common simp-normal form. TerminatesIffRat therefore has to add `attribute [local simp] Pair.map IntFractPair.mapFr`, which makes simp unfold `mapFr` into a structure literal. A global lemma like `mapFr_mk` would make the interface independent of that unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mapFr_b`, `@[simp] theorem mapFr_fr` and `@[simp] theorem mapFr_mk (f : K → β) (b : ℤ) (fr : K) : mapFr f ⟨b, fr⟩ = ⟨b, f fr⟩ := rfl`. Alternatively, tag the definition `@[simps]`. Then drop the local `attribute [local simp] ... IntFractPair.mapFr` in TerminatesIffRat.
findings.benefit: Simp can compute with `mapFr` and with the coercion `coeFn` (which unfolds to `mapFr (↑)`) without a file-local attribute that unfolds the definition. The unfolding stays behind explicit projection lemmas, as `Pair.map` could also do.

evidence.excerpt: def coeFn : IntFractPair K → IntFractPair β := mapFr (↑)
